_note: The COORDINATOR translation — each surface's PRIVATE readiness report → the ONE unified `screen.*` vocabulary (reference/screen-lifecycle.md). THE LAW ENCODED HERE: (1) there are exactly TWO phases — `screen.loading` and `screen.ready`; a failed load is SETTLED, so `surface.domFail` translates identically to `surface.domFinish` (no stuck spinner). (2) The web surface's siblings are `surface.domStart` / `surface.domFinish` / `surface.domFail` (payload { url, surface }); the NATIVE surface's siblings are `surface.viewStart` / `surface.viewFinish` (payload { path, surface: "native", frame }) — the native reporter has no `*Fail` sibling because a native frame ALWAYS settles (first render, or its own `dsx.screen.settled()`); a native screen's failure is a value on the error plane (`dsx.error`), never a lifecycle phase. (3) The APP-SURFACE guard: a report is translated only when its `surface` is the app surface — "web" (the composed app web view) or "native" (a DSXView frame). Any other tag is a BARE embedded surface (a node-owned `<WebView/>`, named by its node) and is DROPPED, so an embedded player loading a page can never flip the app's spinner/splash/analytics. An UNTAGGED payload counts as the app surface (fail-open, Article 7) — the legacy bare-string input keeps working. (4) The re-fired `screen.*` input is the plain ROUTE STRING, never the relay dict: `url` when present, else `path`, else the input itself when it is already a string, else null. Consumers read it as an optional string (PostHog reads it; Spinner et al. ignore it). (5) State rides every translation: `global.screen.frame` (the REPORTING frame id, or null when the report names none — the web relay is frameless) + `global.screen.phase` ("loading" | "ready") + `global.screen.ready` (Bool), published in THAT order and all BEFORE the `screen.*` event fires, so an event hook reads a consistent triple. `screen.frame` is the settle IDENTITY: a consumer that must know WHOSE readiness a report carries — the ROOT PLAN binds each report to the attempt that mounted the frame (root-plan.md §5) — reads it instead of inferring from the level. A DROPPED report (a bare embedded surface) publishes NOTHING, identity included. All three keys are MERGED into the `screen` object that also carries the window metrics (width/height/sizeClass/orientation/breakpoint) — a rotation must never wipe `phase`/`ready`, and a phase publish must never wipe the metrics. (6) The coordinator is STATELESS and level-triggered: it never dedupes, never orders, never remembers — de-duplication is the REPORTER's job (readiness.json rule 5). Executors: Swift `Mandatory/Lifecycle/swift/Lifecycle.swift` · Kotlin `Mandatory/Lifecycle/kotlin/Lifecycle.kt` · TS `packages/kernel/src/screen.ts` (the web renderer ships no Lifecycle module — its kernel publishes `screen.*` directly from the same table, which is why this file, not the module, is the law).

surfaces.web: the composed app WKWebView / WebView — reports surface.domStart · surface.domFinish · surface.domFail
surfaces.native: a DSXView frame in the app's nav.stack — reports surface.viewStart · surface.viewFinish
surfaces.<node name>: a bare embedded <WebView/> — reports dom* tagged with its node name; NEVER translated

cases.name: a web navigation: start then finish
a failed web load is still settled
a native frame: start then settle — the same two fires, no web view involved
a native frame that has only started leaves the shell loading
a native push after a settled screen returns the shell to loading, then ready
a hybrid app: a native frame and a web navigation share one vocabulary
an embedded bare <WebView/> never moves the app's phase
an embedded surface loading UNDER a settled app screen leaves it settled
an UNTAGGED payload is the app surface — fail-open
a legacy BARE STRING input rides through as the route
a routeless report still fires — the input is simply null
url wins over path when a payload carries both
the coordinator is stateless — a duplicate settle republishes without harm
the phase publish MERGES into screen.* — window metrics survive
a report names its frame — a LATE settle from a covered screen is identifiable
